title: Speed distributions of O₂ and H₂ at 300 K
caption: At the same temperature both gases have the same mean kinetic energy, so v_rms ∝ 1/√m. O₂ has v_rms = 484 m s⁻¹ and H₂ 1927 m s⁻¹, a ratio of 4.0 (the lesson's √(32/2) = 4). H₂'s curve is lower and wider because the area under each is 1. Peaks: v_p = 395 and 1573 m s⁻¹.
alt: Two Maxwell–Boltzmann curves: O2 with a tall narrow peak near 395 m/s and H2 with a low wide peak near 1573 m/s.
description: The horizontal axis is molecular speed in m s⁻¹; the vertical axis is f(v) in 10⁻³ s m⁻¹, so each curve has area 1.
O₂ (32 u): peak at v_p = √(2k_BT/m) = 395 m s⁻¹, v_rms = 484 m s⁻¹.
H₂ (2 u): peak at 1573 m s⁻¹, v_rms = 1927 m s⁻¹, 4.0 times faster, so the curve is lower and wider.
